---
title: "AlphaGenome motif-importance analysis"
subtitle: "EVN, SVN, and EVS | held-out chr2 | real genomic backgrounds"
params:
  result_branch: "tangermeme_clustered"
  analysis_label: "Fixed-window seqlet selection"
  include_logos: false
  motif_logo_manifest: ""
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    number_sections: true
    theme: cosmo
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE,
                      fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6, dpi=130)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(gt)
  library(jsonlite)
  library(scales)
  library(tidyr)
})
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size=12) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(), legend.position="bottom"))

task_labels <- c(evn="EVN", svn="SVN", evs="EVS")
task_definitions <- c(
  EVN="Enhancer versus genomic background",
  SVN="Silencer versus genomic background",
  EVS="Enhancer versus silencer"
)
task_colors <- c(EVN="#0072B2", SVN="#D55E00", EVS="#009E73")
sign_colors <- c(negative="#7B3294", positive="#008837")

read_task <- function(task) {
  root <- file.path("results", task, "GRCh38", "alphagenome", "real",
                    params$result_branch, "through_chrX")
  required <- c("metadata.json", "audit.json", "candidate_region_tests.tsv",
                "motif_cluster_summary.tsv", "motif_annotation_summary.tsv",
                "ism_validation.tsv")
  missing <- required[!file.exists(file.path(root, required))]
  if (length(missing)) stop(task, " is missing: ", paste(missing, collapse=", "))
  label <- unname(task_labels[[task]])
  logo_manifest_path <- file.path(root, "attribution_logo_manifest.tsv")
  logo_manifest <- if (file.exists(logo_manifest_path)) {
    read.delim(logo_manifest_path, check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE) |>
      mutate(Task=.env$label,
             image_path=file.path(.env$root, svg))
  } else {
    tibble()
  }
  list(
    root=root,
    metadata=read_json(file.path(root, "metadata.json"), simplifyVector=TRUE),
    audit=read_json(file.path(root, "audit.json"), simplifyVector=TRUE),
    candidates=read.delim(file.path(root, "candidate_region_tests.tsv"),
                          check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE) |>
      mutate(Task=.env$label,
             important_region=important_region %in% c(TRUE, "True", "TRUE", 1)),
    motifs=read.delim(file.path(root, "motif_cluster_summary.tsv"),
                     check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE) |>
      mutate(Task=.env$label,
             enriched_cluster=enriched_cluster %in% c(TRUE, "True", "TRUE", 1)),
    annotation_summary=read.delim(
      file.path(root, "motif_annotation_summary.tsv"),
      check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE
    ) |>
      mutate(Task=.env$label),
    ism=read.delim(file.path(root, "ism_validation.tsv"),
                   check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE) |>
      mutate(Task=.env$label),
    logos=logo_manifest
  )
}

analyses <- setNames(lapply(names(task_labels), read_task), unname(task_labels))
candidates <- bind_rows(lapply(analyses, `[[`, "candidates"))
motifs <- bind_rows(lapply(analyses, `[[`, "motifs"))
annotation_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(analyses, `[[`, "annotation_summary"))
for (column in c("all_signs_n_sequences", "all_signs_median_attribution",
                 "all_signs_attribution_q25", "all_signs_attribution_q75")) {
  if (!column %in% names(annotation_summary)) annotation_summary[[column]] <- NA_real_
}
ism <- bind_rows(lapply(analyses, `[[`, "ism"))
attribution_logos <- bind_rows(lapply(analyses, `[[`, "logos"))
motif_logos <- if (isTRUE(params$include_logos) &&
                   nzchar(params$motif_logo_manifest) &&
                   file.exists(params$motif_logo_manifest)) {
  read.delim(params$motif_logo_manifest, check.names=FALSE,
             stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
} else {
  tibble()
}

logo_gallery <- function(data, image_column, caption_function, card_width="47%") {
  cards <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(data)), function(i) {
    row <- data[i, , drop=FALSE]
    htmltools::tags$figure(
      style=paste0("display:inline-block; width:", card_width,
                   "; vertical-align:top; margin:1%;"),
      htmltools::tags$img(
        src=knitr::image_uri(row[[image_column]][[1]]),
        style="width:100%; height:auto;"
      ),
      htmltools::tags$figcaption(
        style="font-size:0.9em; text-align:center;",
        caption_function(row)
      )
    )
  })
  htmltools::tagList(cards)
}

selection_methods <- unique(vapply(analyses, function(x) {
  value <- x$metadata$parameters$seqlet_selection
  if (is.null(value)) "fixed" else value
}, character(1)))
if (length(selection_methods) != 1) stop("Tasks use different seqlet-selection methods")
selection_method <- selection_methods[[1]]
selection_description <- if (selection_method == "modisco") {
  "TF-MoDISco seqlet calling with a 21-bp attribution window and 10-bp flanks on each side (41-bp returned seqlets)"
} else if (selection_method == "recursive") {
  "Tangermeme recursive variable-length seqlet calling"
} else {
  "Fixed 21-bp non-overlapping attribution windows"
}
candidate_caps <- unique(vapply(analyses, function(x) {
  as.integer(x$metadata$parameters$max_candidate_sites)
}, integer(1)))
if (length(candidate_caps) != 1) stop("Tasks use different candidate caps")
candidate_cap <- candidate_caps[[1]]
candidate_quota <- candidate_cap %/% 4

qc <- bind_rows(lapply(names(analyses), function(task) {
  x <- analyses[[task]]
  tibble(
    Task=task,
    Classification=task_definitions[[task]],
    `Test sequences`=x$metadata$dataset$n_sequences,
    AUROC=x$metadata$performance_on_sample$auroc,
    `Average precision`=x$metadata$performance_on_sample$average_precision,
    `Attribution method`=x$metadata$selected_attribution_method,
    `DeepLIFT relative error`=x$audit$deeplift$relative_error,
    `Candidates tested`=x$metadata$counts$tested_candidate_windows,
    `Important regions`=x$metadata$counts$important_regions,
    `ISM median correlation`=median(x$ism$pearson_position_correlation),
    `ISM correlations below 0.5`=sum(x$ism$pearson_position_correlation < .5)
  )
}))

top_motif_plot <- function(task, n=10) {
  d <- motifs |>
    filter(Task == task, n_sites >= 2) |>
    arrange(desc(n_important_regions), desc(abs(mean_ablation_delta))) |>
    slice_head(n=n) |>
    mutate(label=paste0(representative_gene, " (", sign, ")"),
           label=factor(label, levels=rev(unique(label))))
  ggplot(d, aes(mean_ablation_delta, label, color=sign, size=n_sites)) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin=bootstrap_ci_low, xmax=bootstrap_ci_high),
                   height=.16, linewidth=.7) +
    geom_point(alpha=.9) +
    geom_vline(xintercept=0, color="grey35", linewidth=.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values=sign_colors) +
    scale_size_continuous(range=c(2.5, 7), breaks=pretty_breaks(4)) +
    labs(title=paste(task, "leading annotated motif clusters"),
         subtitle="Ranked by significant regions and effect magnitude; intervals are bootstrap CIs",
         x="Mean native minus ablated logit", y=NULL,
         color="Attribution sign", size="Sites")
}
```

# Scope

This report summarizes motif-level interpretation of the final AlphaGenome
models trained through chrX. Attribution is calculated across every held-out
chr2 test sequence. Region selection uses `r selection_description`. The
`r comma(candidate_cap)` strongest regions are selected with equal
representation from the four combinations of class label and attribution sign
(`r comma(candidate_quota)` regions per stratum).
Each selected region is compared with four class- and length-matched control
windows and evaluated with 20 dinucleotide-shuffle ablations.

HOCOMOCO v14 CORE clustered motifs provide non-redundant labels. Motif labels
are the closest TOMTOM matches to attributed regions; they are model-based
annotations and do not establish transcription-factor occupancy in vivo.

# Quality control

```{r qc-table}
qc |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title="Analysis and attribution quality control") |>
  fmt_integer(columns=c(`Test sequences`, `Candidates tested`, `Important regions`,
                        `ISM correlations below 0.5`)) |>
  fmt_number(columns=c(AUROC, `Average precision`, `DeepLIFT relative error`,
                       `ISM median correlation`), decimals=3)
```

DeepLIFT failed its summation-to-delta audit for all three AlphaGenome
classifiers because the backbone contains operations without valid DeepLIFT
rules. The workflow therefore selected saliency automatically. Prediction
parity between the wrapped and native model was exact for every task.

```{r ism, fig.height=4.8}
ggplot(ism, aes(Task, pearson_position_correlation, color=Task)) +
  geom_boxplot(width=.45, outlier.shape=NA, alpha=.12) +
  geom_jitter(width=.12, height=0, alpha=.65, size=1.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=.5, linetype="dashed", color="grey35") +
  scale_color_manual(values=task_colors, guide="none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title="Saliency agreement with in-silico mutagenesis",
       subtitle="Pearson correlation across positions for 40 selected sequences per task",
       x=NULL, y="Position-level correlation")
```

# Candidate design

```{r candidate-balance}
candidates |>
  count(Task, label, sign, name="Regions") |>
  mutate(Class=if_else(label == 1, "Positive class", "Negative class"),
         Task=factor(Task, levels=c("EVN", "SVN", "EVS"))) |>
  select(Task, Class, `Attribution sign`=sign, Regions) |>
  gt(groupname_col="Task") |>
  tab_header(title="Balanced candidate panel") |>
  fmt_integer(columns=Regions)
```

All test sequences contribute to the attribution screen. The candidate cap
restricts only the expensive perturbation analysis. Consequently, absence from
the following tables means “not detected among the strongest tested regions,”
not that a model never uses the motif.

# Motif prevalence across all attributed regions

```{r all-region-top-motifs}
top_annotation_clusters <- annotation_summary |>
  group_by(Task, representative_motif, representative_gene) |>
  summarise(
    Regions=first(all_signs_n_sites),
    Sequences=first(all_signs_n_sequences),
    `Median attribution`=first(all_signs_median_attribution),
    `Attribution Q25`=first(all_signs_attribution_q25),
    `Attribution Q75`=first(all_signs_attribution_q75),
    .groups="drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(Task) |>
  slice_max(Regions, n=20, with_ties=FALSE) |>
  arrange(Task, desc(Regions)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Motif=if_else(is.na(representative_gene) |
                         representative_gene == "",
                       representative_motif, representative_gene))

top_annotation_clusters |>
  select(Task, Motif, Regions, Sequences, `Median attribution`,
         `Attribution Q25`, `Attribution Q75`) |>
  gt(groupname_col="Task") |>
  tab_header(
    title="Twenty most frequently matched HOCOMOCO clusters per task",
    subtitle="Counts use every annotated recursive seqlet, before ablation selection"
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns=c(Regions, Sequences)) |>
  fmt_number(columns=c(`Median attribution`, `Attribution Q25`,
                       `Attribution Q75`), decimals=2)
```

This descriptive inventory is independent of the strongest-region ablation
panel. A frequent cluster can therefore remain biologically interesting even
when its individual regions have moderate attribution or are not represented
among the strongest ablated sites.

  group_by(Task) |>
  arrange(desc(n_important_regions), desc(abs(mean_ablation_delta)), .by_group=TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n=10) |>

top_table |>

```{r logos, results='asis'}
if (isTRUE(params$include_logos)) {
  cat("# Model-derived and reference motif logos\n\n")
  cat("Each panel aligns the tested regions assigned to a motif and averages their signed nucleotide contributions after correcting for motif orientation. The paired HOCOMOCO PWM is the reference motif used for annotation. Individual sequence-level attribution logos remain available as quality-control artifacts but are omitted here.\n\n")
  for (task in c("EVN", "SVN", "EVS")) {
    cat("## ", task, " leading motif logos\n\n", sep="")

    if (nrow(task_motifs)) {

        function(row) paste0(
          row$representative_gene, " (", row$sign, "); ",

          " important regions",
          if (isTRUE(row$enriched_cluster[[1]])) "; class-enriched" else ""
        ),
        card_width="98%"
      ))
    }
  }
}
```

# Descriptive comparison across tasks

The models were trained for different classification problems and are explained
on their native held-out data. The comparison below is therefore descriptive:
it highlights recurring motif clusters, while effect magnitudes should not be
treated as directly calibrated between models.

The bars summarize only the selected ablation panel, not every seqlet called
across the test set. When a task contains both positive- and
negative-attribution occurrences of the same motif, the plot retains the sign
with more significant regions (then more sampled sites as a tie-breaker) so
that each task contributes at most one bar per motif.

```{r recurring-sites-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
recurring_genes <- motifs |>
  filter(n_sites >= 2) |>
  distinct(Task, representative_gene) |>
  count(representative_gene, name="Tasks") |>
  filter(Tasks >= 2) |>
  pull(representative_gene)

recurring_all <- motifs |>
  filter(representative_gene %in% recurring_genes,
         n_sites >= 2) |>
  mutate(Motif=representative_gene)

top_recurring_genes <- recurring_all |>
  group_by(Motif) |>
  summarise(total_sites=sum(n_sites), .groups="drop") |>
  arrange(desc(total_sites), Motif) |>
  slice_head(n=20) |>
  pull(Motif)

recurring_plot <- recurring_all |>
  filter(Motif %in% top_recurring_genes) |>
  group_by(Task, Motif) |>
  arrange(desc(n_important_regions), desc(n_sites),
          desc(abs(mean_ablation_delta)), .by_group=TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n=1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    Task=factor(Task, levels=names(task_colors)),
    Motif=factor(Motif, levels=rev(top_recurring_genes)),
    signed_sites=if_else(sign == "negative", -n_sites, n_sites)
  )

if (nrow(recurring_plot)) {
  label_offset <- max(abs(recurring_plot$signed_sites), na.rm=TRUE) * .035
  recurring_plot <- recurring_plot |>
    mutate(label_y=signed_sites + if_else(signed_sites >= 0,
                                          label_offset, -label_offset))
  ggplot(recurring_plot,
         aes(Motif, signed_sites, fill=Task, group=Task)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept=0, color="grey30", linewidth=.55) +
    geom_col(position=position_dodge(width=.82), width=.74) +
    geom_text(aes(y=label_y, label=n_important_regions),
              position=position_dodge(width=.82), size=3.1, color="grey15",
              vjust=.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=task_colors, drop=FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels=function(x) comma(abs(x)),
                       expand=expansion(mult=c(.12, .12))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip="off") +
    labs(
      title="Most frequently sampled recurring motif clusters",
      subtitle=paste0(
        "Top 20 by combined sampled sites across tasks.\n",
        "Negative-attribution sites extend below zero; labels count significant ablation-supported regions."
      ),
      x="Motif cluster", y="Number of sites", fill="Task"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1),
      plot.margin=margin(10, 14, 10, 10)
    )
} else {
  cat("No motif cluster met the reporting criteria in more than one task.")
}
```

# Class-enriched motif clusters

Class enrichment is calculated only within the balanced, selected candidate
panel. It is not a genome-wide motif-enrichment test and is kept separate from
the causal ablation result.

```{r enrichment-table}
enriched <- motifs |>
  filter(enriched_cluster) |>
  transmute(Task, Motif=representative_gene, Sign=sign, Sites=n_sites,
            `Important regions`=n_important_regions,
            `Positive-class sequences`=n_positive_sequences,
            `Negative-class sequences`=n_negative_sequences,
            `Adjusted enrichment p-value`=enrichment_adjusted_pvalue,
            `Mean ablation effect`=mean_ablation_delta)

if (nrow(enriched)) {
  enriched |>
    gt(groupname_col="Task") |>
    tab_header(title="Class-enriched clusters within the selected panel") |>
    fmt_integer(columns=c(Sites, `Important regions`, `Positive-class sequences`,
                          `Negative-class sequences`)) |>
    fmt_scientific(columns=`Adjusted enrichment p-value`, decimals=2) |>
    fmt_number(columns=`Mean ablation effect`, decimals=2)
} else {
  cat("No motif cluster was class-enriched after multiple-testing correction.")
}
```

# Interpretation

EVN and SVN provide the strongest basis for biological hypothesis generation
because their held-out classification performance and saliency–ISM agreement
are high. EVS can still reveal potentially interesting sequence features, but
its more modest predictive performance makes those findings exploratory.

Repeated motif families across tasks are candidates for shared regulatory
grammar. Task-restricted clusters are candidates for task-specific mechanisms,
but their apparent absence elsewhere is conditional on the strongest-region candidate
design. Ablation estimates how editing a selected region changes the model
prediction; the `important region` label additionally requires that effect to
exceed matched controls after multiple-testing correction. Neither result
establishes TF binding or causal regulation in cells.
